name: v2.5.0
body:
The `v2.5.0` release is a regular quarterly Crossplane release that is focused on maturing a number of key areas of functionality across the project, as Crossplane continues to become more capable, more reliable, and more performant for your production workloads. This release includes function-controlled deletion, referencing functions by OCI digest, garbage collection of unused `CompositionRevisions`, lower memory usage, security hardening, and a wide range of fixes and reliability improvements. It also includes security fixes in Crossplane's Go toolchain and dependencies.

# 🚨 v1.20 end-of-life (EOL)

**With the release of v2.5, v1.20 has reached its EOL and will no longer receive any support or maintenance by the Crossplane project**. [`v1.20.15`](https://github.com/crossplane/crossplane/releases/tag/v1.20.15) is the final release of v1.20.

> [!IMPORTANT] 
> This EOL notice applies only to the v1.20 release. v1 legacy workloads like Claims and cluster scoped resources remain supported in Crossplane v2 through extensive [backwards compatibility support](https://docs.crossplane.io/latest/guides/upgrade-to-crossplane-v2/#legacy-resource-behavior).

## Is your control plane ready for v2?

Upgrading to Crossplane v2 does not require any migration as part of the upgrade process, with the exception of the minimal breaking changes explicitly called out in the [v2 documentation](https://docs.crossplane.io/latest/guides/upgrade-to-crossplane-v2/#removed-features). If your control plane is not affected by those changes, you can simply [upgrade to v2](https://docs.crossplane.io/latest/guides/upgrade-crossplane/) right away.

To better assist Crossplane users in determining if their control planes are affected by any of the breaking changes in v2, we have released a v2 readiness checker tool in the v1.20 Crossplane CLI that can be invoked via `crossplane beta upgrade check`. You can read all about this tool in the following resources:

* blog post: [https://blog.crossplane.io/v2-upgrade-check/](https://blog.crossplane.io/v2-upgrade-check/)   
* docs: [https://docs.crossplane.io/v1.20/cli/command-reference/\#beta-upgrade-check](https://docs.crossplane.io/v1.20/cli/command-reference/#beta-upgrade-check)   
* release notes: [https://github.com/crossplane/crossplane/releases/tag/v1.20.9](https://github.com/crossplane/crossplane/releases/tag/v1.20.9) 

## Crossplane Downstream Distributions

Downstream distributions are eligible to continue their extended support and maintenance for their releases that are based on upstream Crossplane's v1.20. Check with your [vendor](https://www.crossplane.io/commercial) for more details if you are using a downstream distribution of Crossplane.

# ⚠️ Upgrade from `v2.4`

It is strongly advised to upgrade to `v2.5` from the previous minor version, which is `v2.4`.  Upon upgrade for each minor release, Crossplane performs any necessary migrations of its CRDs to ensure the latest versions are stored in the Kubernetes API server. Therefore, it is important to upgrade sequentially through one minor version at a time as described in the [upgrade docs](https://docs.crossplane.io/latest/guides/upgrade-crossplane/).

# 🚨 v2.5 Notable and Breaking Changes

* ⚠️ `status.crossplane` is now reserved for Crossplane on modern XRs, the same way `spec.crossplane` already is. 
  * Crossplane records its own state there, starting with `status.crossplane.deletionPolicy`, and replaces any `status.crossplane` an XRD's schema declares.
  * If your XRD declares its own fields under `status.crossplane`, move them to a different status field before upgrading. 
  * Legacy XRs are unaffected.
  * See crossplane/crossplane-runtime#1226 for related change.

# 🎉 Highlights

* **Function-controlled deletion (alpha):** Your composition functions can now decide when and in what order an XR's composed resources are deleted, enabling ordered teardown and custom deletion hooks, which is a long standing feature request tracked in #5092. 
  * A new `Composition` field `spec.deletionPolicy` lets you specify the deletion behavior:
    * `Background` (the default) keeps today's behavior
    * `Foreground` keeps the XR alive until all composed resources are deleted completely
    * `Pipeline` keeps running your functions during deletion so they decide how/when to delete their composed resources
  * `crossplane internal render` can also render an XR's deletion so you can see it play out locally.
  * Enable it with `--enable-function-controlled-deletion`. See the [design](https://github.com/crossplane/crossplane/blob/main/design/one-pager-function-controlled-deletion.md), #8000 and #8012.
* **Reference functions by OCI digest (alpha):** Pipeline steps in a `Composition` or `Operation` can now reference a function package directly by digest with the new `function` field, instead of a `functionRef` by name to an installed `Function`.
  * Crossplane installs the function for you, and several versions of the same function can run side by side.
  * Each `CompositionRevision` pins the exact function versions it calls, so a function upgrade no longer changes the behavior of every XR at once and can be rolled out progressively like any other composition change.
  * Enable it with `--enable-pipeline-oci-references`. See the [design](https://github.com/crossplane/crossplane/blob/main/design/one-pager-controlled-rollout-of-composition-functions-v2.md) and #7840, fixing #6139.
* **Garbage collection of unused `CompositionRevisions` (alpha):** Crossplane can now garbage collect `CompositionRevisions` that are no longer in use, instead of that list continuing to grow forever.
  * With `--enable-composition-revision-gc`, Crossplane deletes unused revisions beyond the new `spec.unusedRevisionHistoryLimit` field on `Composition` (default `1`, and `0` keeps every revision).
  * The latest revision and any revision in use by an XR are always kept. #7916, closing #4837.
* **Lighter on memory and the API server:** 
  * Crossplane no longer caches the OpenAPI schema of every CRD in the cluster, which cut heap usage from 338 MiB to 190 MiB and RSS from 415 MiB to 250 MiB on a cluster with 791 CRDs (#7955).
  * The MRD, MRAP and `PackageRevision` controllers stopped rewriting unchanged status on every sync (#7851), and `Usages` no longer rewrite the in-use label on every reconcile (#7860).
* **Optional function credentials:** Set `resolvePolicy: Optional` on a pipeline step's credential and the function runs without it when the `Secret` doesn't exist, instead of simply failing the pipeline completely. If your function can work with or without credentials, then use this setting to ensure your function is run either way. #6994
* **Security hardening:** Several fixes focus on tightening code paths where a caller could reach further than intended.
    * A namespaced XR can no longer compose a cluster scoped resource by having a function set `metadata.namespace` on it. #8050
    * The RBAC manager builds generated `ClusterRoles` only from CRDs actually owned by the `ProviderRevision` or XRD, and removes stale grants on every reconcile. #8054
    * The RBAC manager only binds a provider's `ServiceAccount` when its runtime `Deployment` is in Crossplane's namespace and is controlled by the exact `ProviderRevision`. #8055
    * A claim that can't look up its XRD now fails reconciliation, so it can't bypass an XRD's `enforcedCompositionRef`. #7789
    * Crossplane now builds with Go 1.26 (#7802), alongside security updates to Crossplane's dependencies across this release cycle.
* **Other notable improvements**:
    * New Helm values `webhooks.usage.failurePolicy` (`Fail` or `Ignore`) and `usages.enabled` let you relax or remove the `Usage` webhook, which previously blocked Azure AKS cluster stop on clusters running Crossplane. #7784
    * `crossplane-edit` and `crossplane-admin` users can now `kubectl scale` XRs and claims whose XRD serves the scale subresource. #7922
    * Providers and other packages with `packagePullPolicy: Always` no longer download the package again every minute when its tag still points to the same digest. Previously a slow registry could mark healthy Providers `Unhealthy`. crossplane/crossplane-runtime#1242, fixing #7984.
    * A new package revision now reliably takes ownership of its objects during upgrades, which could previously leave it unhealthy with no runtime. #7733, #7839
    * An `ImageConfig` that only sets a runtime config is now applied right away instead of on the next resync. #7970
    * `DeploymentRuntimeConfig` has a `drc` short name. #8006
    * `Operations` now record how many resources they applied in `status.appliedResources`, shown in the `APPLIED` column of `kubectl get operations`. #7885, backported in #8075.

## 🏅 Release MVP

For the v2.5 release cycle, we'd like to recognize @sarankumar1325 as the release MVP!

They fixed a frustrating problem for anyone using `packagePullPolicy: Always`: Crossplane downloaded the package again every minute even when nothing had changed, so a slow registry could mark perfectly healthy Providers as `Unhealthy`. Their fix in https://github.com/crossplane/crossplane-runtime/pull/1242 serves the package from the cache whenever the tag still resolves to the same digest. They also contributed fixes in `provider-gitlab` that stop approval rules from being updated on every poll (https://github.com/crossplane-contrib/provider-gitlab/pull/482) and stop projects pending deletion from being renamed back (https://github.com/crossplane-contrib/provider-gitlab/pull/483).

Thank you for your impact on the Crossplane ecosystem @sarankumar1325! 🙇‍♂️
